title: Bench par Tumhara Pehla Agent, Skill aur Tools
summary: Frappe bench par AI-SDLC system ke pehle working pieces banao aur test karo: ek reviewer subagent (v1 snapshot ke roop mein rakha jaata hai jise aage ke modules improve aur evaluate karte hain), ek explain-endpoint skill jo spice_lite whitelisted method ko /api/method route se us SQL tak trace karti hai jo Frappe sach mein bhejta hai, aur ek run-tests skill jo pre-approved commands aur ek tested parser ke saath bench run-tests chalati hai, kyonki tests fail hone par bhi bench 0 se exit karta hai. Phir ek subagent-scoped Claude Code hook se reviewer ke tools restrict karo jo bench console, execute aur migrate block karta hai, aur sab kuch claude -p se headless test karo.
prerequisites: Ek working bench jisme spice_lite test.localhost par installed ho (`AI-SDLC-frappe/sample-app/scripts/setup-bench.sh`); `bench --site test.localhost run-tests --app spice_lite` 46 tests pass karta hai
Claude Code CLI installed aur authenticated (`claude --version`)
PATH par Python 3.11 aur Node 22; `jq` installed (`--output-format json` results padhta hai)

concepts.heading: Subagent file ki anatomy
concepts.body_md:
Subagent **YAML frontmatter wali ek Markdown file** hai. Do keys required hain:

- `name`: identity (`reviewer`). Filename ka match hona zaroori nahi, aur subfolders ise nahi badalte. Claude Code hooks ise `agent_type` ke roop mein dekhte hain.
- `description`: Claude ko kab delegate karna chahiye. Main session kaam route karne ke liye har description padhta hai, isliye ise trigger ki tarah likho: kya karta hai aur kab ("Reviews code changes in the spice_lite Frappe app. Use after code changes.").

Is module mein use hone wali optional keys: `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model` (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, poora id, ya `inherit`), `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `hooks`. Subagent keys **camelCase** hain. Unknown keys **chupchaap ignore** hoti hain: agent file mein `allowed-tools:` (skill wali spelling) ya `max_turns:` kuch nahi karta aur koi error nahi deta.

### File kahan rehti hai, yeh decide karta hai ki kise milti hai

Ek hi `name` ke liye upar wali entry jeet-ti hai: managed settings `.claude/agents/` > `--agents` JSON flag > project `.claude/agents/` (working directory ke sabse paas) > `~/.claude/agents/` > plugin `agents/`. Practically:

- Team agents `AI-SDLC-frappe/.claude/agents/` mein rehte hain aur code ki tarah review hote hain, us DocType JSON ke bagal mein jise woh review karte hain.
- `--agents '{...}'` **test harness** hai: yeh file chhue bina ek session ke liye project agent ko override karta hai.
- Do versions side by side ke liye do naam chahiye. Finished repository mein pehle se module 05 ka `reviewer` hai, isliye yeh module v1 ko `reviewer-v1` ke roop mein install karta hai.

Nayi files hot-reload hoti hain, siwaay nayi bani `agents` directory ke pehle agent ke, jise restart chahiye.

concepts.heading: Body hi poora system prompt hai
concepts.body_md:
Markdown body us subagent ke liye Claude Code system prompt ko **replace** karta hai. Start-up par use sirf milta hai: uska body, main session ka likha task message, CLAUDE.md hierarchy, git status, basic environment details, aur `skills:` mein listed koi bhi skills. Use tumhari conversation, output style ya auto memory **nahi** milti.

Frappe codebase par iska matlab hai ki agent ko pata hai bench kahan hai (`/home/user/frappe-bench`), kaunsi site safe hai (`test.localhost`) aur ki `site_config.json` off limits hai, sirf isliye kyonki `AI-SDLC-frappe/CLAUDE.md` aisa kehti hai. Use pata hai ki DocType JSON, `hooks.py` aur `patches.txt` change ka hissa hain, sirf tab jab body use batata hai.

### Ise likhna

- **Pehle role aur scope**: "`sample-app/spice_lite/` mein `spice_lite` app ka senior Frappe aur Python code reviewer". Specialization hi subagent ko `general-purpose` se behtar banata hai.
- **Ek procedure** jise woh bina guess kiye follow kar sake: `git diff HEAD -- sample-app`, badli hui files padho *aur* agar chhue gaye hon toh DocType JSON aur `hooks.py`, named standards check karo.
- **Path se repository awareness**: `context/standards/frappe-coding-standards.md` aur `review-standards.md` ko paste karne ki jagah unka naam lo.
- **Ek output format** jise koi parse kar sake. v1 sirf "report the problems you find" kehta hai, aur kuch nahi. Yeh jaan-boojh kar hai: module `09-agent-evaluation` ko ek naive baseline chahiye.

Body ka har sentence us agent ke har turn par tokens khata hai. Jo facts har agent ko chahiye woh CLAUDE.md mein jaate hain; body mein role, procedure aur output rehta hai.

concepts.heading: Bench par tool selection: allowlists, aur console aur execute alag kyon hain
concepts.body_md:
`tools` ek **allowlist** hai. Ise **chhod do** toh subagent har woh tool inherit karta hai jo subagents ko available hai, MCP tools samet. Reviewer v1 yahi karta hai, isliye ek "reviewer" Edit, Write kar sakta hai, aur jo bhi Bash permission rules allow karein chala sakta hai.

`disallowedTools` ek **denylist** hai, aur specifier tool ko narrow nahi karta: `disallowedTools: Bash(bench *)` **poora** Bash hata deta hai. Tool list se tum Bash ko scope nahi kar sakte.

Bench par Bash ek tool nahi, bahut alag blast radius wala ek parivaar hai:

| Command | Kya kar sakta hai |
|---|---|
| `bench --site test.localhost run-tests` | `FrappeTestCase` classes chalata hai, jo har class ke baad roll back hoti hain; Link targets ke test records commit hote hain |
| `bench --site test.localhost list-apps` | read-only |
| `bench --site X console` | Administrator ke roop mein IPython shell: koi bhi Python, koi bhi SQL, koi permission checks nahi |
| `bench --site X execute <dotted.fn>` | koi bhi function Administrator ke roop mein call karta hai aur **commit** karta hai (`spice_lite.demo.seed_demo` API secrets rotate karta hai) |
| `bench --site X migrate` | DocType JSON sync karta hai, `patches.txt` chalata hai, shared site ka schema badalta hai |

`console` aur `execute` isliye khatarnaak hain kyonki woh *site par sabse oonchi privilege ke saath general-purpose code execution* hain, isliye nahi ki agent ka intent kya hai. `AI-SDLC-frappe/.claude/settings.json` unhe `ask` ke under rakhta hai; `drop-site` aur `reinstall` ko `deny` ke under.

Isliye practically: read-only agents ko `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash` aur ek Claude Code hook milta hai jo Bash ko named commands tak narrow karta hai; code review karne wali kisi cheez ko `console` ya `execute` ki zaroorat nahi. Tool list batati hai *kaunse* tools; Claude Code hooks aur permission rules batate hain *kaunsi calls*.

concepts.heading: Permissions: permissionMode, parent ka mode, aur layered controls
concepts.body_md:
Subagent `permissionMode` declare kar sakta hai: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk` ya `bypassPermissions`. Read-only reviewer ke liye `dontAsk` attractive hai: jo bhi prompt karta woh deny hota hai, aur `permissions.allow` se allowed commands (jaise `.claude/settings.json` mein `Bash(git diff *)` aur `Bash(bench --site test.localhost run-tests *)`) ab bhi chalte hain.

Lekin subagent ka `permissionMode` **ignore hota hai jab parent session `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits` ya `auto` mein chalta hai**, aur subagent `bypassPermissions` tak escalate nahi kar sakta jab tak parent pehle se usme na ho. Recent versions naye terminal sessions `auto` mein start karte hain, isliye tumhari `dontAsk` line aksar effect mein nahi hoti.

Isiliye yeh module controls ko layer karta hai:

1. `tools` woh hata deta hai jo agent kabhi use nahi kar sakta (koi Edit nahi, koi Write nahi).
2. **Agent ke apne frontmatter mein** ek `PreToolUse` Claude Code hook chalta hai, parent chahe kisi bhi mode mein ho. `reviewer-bash-guard.mjs` `git diff/log/show/status` aur safe arguments wale `bench --site test.localhost run-tests` ke alawa sab ke liye 2 se exit karta hai, aur apne message mein `console`, `execute` aur `migrate` ka naam leta hai. Precondition: Claude Code project agent ke frontmatter hooks tabhi chalata hai jab folder ek interactive session mein trusted ho chuka ho; kabhi trusted na hue folder mein `claude -p` run unhe skip karta hai.
3. Settings mein `permissions.deny` (`Read(**/site_config.json)`, `Bash(bench drop-site *)`) har jagah apply hota hai.
4. `permissionMode` aakhri, best-effort layer hai.

Yahan dono tarah ke hook ko confuse mat karo: guard ek **Claude Code hook** hai (Claude Code event par chalne wala Node script). Iska `hooks.py` ke **Frappe hook** se koi lena-dena nahi. Jo agent ab bhi Edit aur Write inherit karta hai uske headless tests ke liye `claude -p ... --permission-mode plan` chalao.

concepts.heading: Context injection: bench par CLAUDE.md, preloaded skills, aur !`cmd`
concepts.body_md:
Kisi agent ya skill ke start hone se **pehle** uske saamne repository knowledge rakhne ke teen tareeke:

- **CLAUDE.md**: har subagent ke liye load hoti hai (built-in Explore aur Plan ko chhod kar). `AI-SDLC-frappe/CLAUDE.md` har agent ko bench path, test command aur PHI rules deti hai.
- **Agent frontmatter mein `skills:`**: listed skills start-up par inject hoti hain. Module 05 tester aur developer ko `skills: [run-tests]` deta hai. `disable-model-invocation: true` wali skill preload nahi ho sakti, isliye run-tests default rakhti hai.
- **SKILL.md body mein `` !`command` ``**: skill invoke hone par chalta hai; uska output placeholder ko replace karta hai. Frappe repo par kaam ke injections woh facts hain jo files mein ya site par rehte hain:
  - `grep -rn -A1 "@frappe.whitelist" sample-app/spice_lite/spice_lite --include=*.py`: har whitelisted method aur uske allowed verbs;
  - `python3 ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doctype_summary.py`: DocType JSON se padhi har DocType ki ek line (naming, `search_index`, `unique`, Links, role ke hisaab se DocPerm rows);
  - `cd /home/user/frappe-bench && bench --site test.localhost list-apps`: prove karta hai ki site aur uska database jawab dete hain, app versions aur branches ke saath.

Sharp edges:

- **Non-zero exit poori skill abort kar deta hai** (`grep` ka exit 1 tolerate hota hai). `bench run-tests` kabhi inject mat karo. `list-apps` inject karna jaan-boojh kar fail-fast hai: agar Postgres down hai toh skill turant ruk jaati hai.
- Command **permission rules ke against check hota hai**; ise skill ke `allowed-tools` mein pre-approve karo. `allowed-tools` pre-approve karta hai, restrict nahi karta.
- Injected JSON facts database ke baare mein galat ho sakte hain. DocType JSON kehta hai ki `SL Encounter.patient` par `search_index: 1` hai; `pg_indexes` aisa koi index nahi dikhata (agla concept). Jo sasta aur sach ho woh inject karo; verified observations ko supporting file mein rakho.

`$ARGUMENTS` poori argument string hai, `$0` pehla argument (0-based), aur `arguments: [module, test]` named `$module` aur `$test` deta hai.

concepts.heading: Observation se bani reference file, memory se nahi
concepts.body_md:
"Is endpoint ko explain karo" wale jawab ka sabse kamzor hissa aksar SQL hota hai: model khushi se `frappe.get_list` ke liye plausible SQL likh dega. `explain-endpoint` skill ise `reference.md` se avoid karti hai, jiska SQL section `docs/tutorials/level-2/tools/capture_sql.py` se **real site par capture** kiya gaya tha. Tool `Database._log_query` ko wrap karta hai (Frappe har executed statement ke baad ise call karta hai; Postgres par isme `cursor.query` hota hai, woh text jo psycopg2 ne bheja), method ko `clinician@spice-lite.test` ke roop mein do baar call karta hai, statements print karta hai aur sab roll back kar deta hai.

Capture ne kya dikhaya, jisme se kuch bhi spice_lite code mein nahi hai:

- `search_patients` bhejta hai `... where "tabSL Patient"."last_name" ilike '<family>%%' ... limit 50 offset 0`: Frappe Postgres par `like` ko `ilike` bana deta hai, aur `EXPLAIN` dikhata hai ki iske liye `last_name` b-tree use nahi hota, jabki `fhir.py:78` ka ek comment kehta hai ki hota hai.
- `lastn` warm process par har subject ke exactly 2 statements leta hai (1 → 2, 2 → 4, 5 → 10), har ek `select *` bina `LIMIT` ke.
- Postgres par har insert `select table_name from information_schema.tables ...` bhi chalata hai: Frappe ka apna `doc_events["*"]["on_update"]` (`frappe/hooks.py:166`) `table_exists` call karta hai, aur Postgres `get_tables()` apna cache flag ignore karta hai.
- `SL Patient.country` aur `SL Encounter.patient` par `search_index: 1` hai lekin **koi index nahi**: Frappe v15 Postgres indexes ka naam bare field name par rakhta hai (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "patient"`), aur woh naam pehle se `tabSL Observation` aur `tabAddress Template` ke the.
- Cold process 9 se 12 statements aur jodta hai (roles, User, User Permissions, DocType meta).

Isliye practically: supporting files **provenance ke saath observations** (command, site, date) rakhti hain, aur skill ke rules kehte hain ki unhe cite karo, ya baaki sab ko "not observed" label karo.

concepts.heading: Headless testing aur iteration
concepts.body_md:
Agent aisa code hai jise tum seedhe unit-test nahi kar sakte, isliye tum fixed inputs par uska behaviour test karte ho. Yahan fixed inputs `docs/tutorials/level-2/patches/` ke do labelled patches hain:

- `02-review-exercise.patch`: `search_patients` ke search terms log karta hai aur `frappe.get_list` ko `frappe.get_all` se badal deta hai. Ise apply karne ke baad bhi **saare 46 tests pass hote hain**. Sirf review ise pakadta hai.
- `02-final-without-value-regression.patch`: `final` Observation ko bina value ke save hone deta hai. Exactly ek test fail hota hai: `TestSLObservation.test_final_requires_value_and_unit`.

Inhe `AI-SDLC-frappe/` se `git apply --directory="$(git rev-parse --show-prefix)" <patch>` ke saath apply karo. Repository ki subdirectory ke andar plain `git apply` un paths ko **skip** kar deta hai jo directory ke bahar resolve hote hain, kuch print nahi karta aur 0 se exit karta hai (`-v` `Skipped patch` dikhata hai).

Runner `claude -p` hai:

| Flag | Kyon |
|---|---|
| `--output-format json` | `result`, `subtype`, `is_error`, `num_turns`, `total_cost_usd`, `session_id`, `usage` |
| `--max-turns 10` | loop ko cap karta hai; limit hit hone par `subtype: error_max_turns` milta hai |
| `--permission-mode plan` | un agents ke liye read-only run jo ab bhi Edit/Write inherit karte hain |
| `--agent reviewer` | agent ko main thread ke roop mein chalao |
| `--agents '{"reviewer": {...}}'` | ek session ke liye agent override karo |
| `--output-format stream-json --verbose` | har message, us `Agent` tool call samet jisne delegate kiya |

`-p` mode mein skill prompt mein `/run-tests` daal kar chalti hai. Loop: **ek** cheez badlo, wahi command usi patch par dobara chalao, `result`, `num_turns` aur `total_cost_usd` compare karo, use `docs/tutorials/level-2/README.md` mein log karo. Jis cheez ko model nahi chahiye woh bina model ke test hoti hai: parser **captured bench output** ke against, Claude Code hook piped JSON ke saath.

02-first-agent-reviewer-v1.title: Reviewer v1 banao aur use headless test karo
02-first-agent-reviewer-v1.objective: Pehla subagent likho, ek jaan-boojh kar simple `reviewer` jisme sirf `name`, `description`, `model` aur ek chhota body ho. Ise module 05 ke reviewer ke bagal mein `reviewer-v1` ke roop mein install karo, ek labelled patch apply karo jise test suite nahi pakadta, aur `claude -p` se prove karo ki main session use delegate karta hai aur woh dono defects dhoondhta hai. `evaluations/agent-versions/reviewer-v1.md` ko unchanged rakho: module 09 ise v2 se compare karta hai.

evaluationCriteria: `description` batata hai ki agent kya karta hai aur use kab delegate karna hai.
Body ek system prompt hai: role, numbered procedure, kahan dekhna hai (`git diff`, DocType JSON, `hooks.py`, CLAUDE.md).
v1 valid hai lekin jaan-boojh kar naive: koi `tools` line nahi aur koi structured output nahi. Snapshot ko improve mat karo; improvements baad ke versions mein jaate hain.
Headless command sirf documented flags use karta hai (`-p`, `--permission-mode`, `--max-turns`, `--output-format`).
Learner samjha sakta hai ki green suite plus prose review is baat ka evidence kyon nahi hai ki change safe hai.
improvements: Wahi command teen baar chalao aur `result` fields diff karo: yahi baseline noise hai jo module 09 measure karta hai.

Files edit kiye bina ek run ke liye agent override karo: `claude -p ... --agents '{"reviewer-v1": {"description": "Reviews spice_lite changes.", "prompt": "You are a reviewer. Reply with findings only.", "tools": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"]}}'`.
`color: blue` jodo taaki interactive session mein reviewer aasani se dikhe.

02-explain-endpoint-skill.title: Real SQL se bani reference file ke saath explain-endpoint skill likho
02-explain-endpoint-skill.objective: `.claude/skills/explain-endpoint/` banao: ek SKILL.md jo `$ARGUMENTS` ke roop mein dotted method ya `/api/method/...` path leti hai, whitelisted-method map, DocType JSON se padhi DocType summary aur request badalne wale Frappe hook keys inject karti hai, aur ek `reference.md` link karti hai jiska SQL `capture_sql.py` se real site par capture kiya gaya. Ise `spice_lite.api.fhir.lastn` par invoke karo aur check karo ki jawab route, whitelist, permissions, controller aur `doc_events`, SQL aur tests ko real `path:line` citations aur 2-statements-per-subject count ke saath trace karta hai.

Har injection sasta hai, fail hone par safe hai (grep exit 1 tolerate hota hai) aur pre-approved hai; kisi ko bench nahi chahiye.

Learner un do framework behaviours ko samjha sakta hai jo capture ne dikhaye (har insert par `information_schema` query, missing Postgres indexes).
improvements: `paths: ["sample-app/spice_lite/**/api/*.py"]` jodo taaki skill sirf tab auto-activate ho jab Claude API code par kaam kare.
Wahi methods MariaDB site (`mariadb.localhost`) par capture karo aur ek column jodo: `ilike` `like` ban jaata hai, aur index names per table hote hain.
Trace ko main context se bahar rakhne ke liye skill ko `context: fork` aur `agent: Explore` ke saath chalao (Explore CLAUDE.md load nahi karta, isliye skill mein bench path ka naam lo).

02-run-tests-skill.title: Agent ko ek tool do: run-tests skill aur bench output ka parser
02-run-tests-skill.objective: `/run-tests [module [test]]` banao: `allowed-tools` se exactly `cd`, `bench --site test.localhost run-tests`, `list-apps`, parser aur `git status` commands pre-approve karo, `!` se `bench list-apps` aur changed files inject karo, named arguments validate karo, aur bench ke output ko ek zero-dependency Python parser se compact verdict mein badlo jo real bench se captured output ke against tested ho. Ise ek labelled regression pakadne ke liye use karo jo final Observation ko bina value ke save hone deta hai.

evaluationCriteria: `allowed-tools` compound command ke har hisse ke liye ek rule list karta hai, YAML list form mein kyonki rules mein spaces hain.
Failing test skill ko abort nahi kar sakta: bench normal Bash call ke roop mein chalta hai, aur sirf `list-apps` aur `git status` inject hote hain.

Verdict parser ke exit code se aata hai, aur learner un teen bench behaviours ka naam le sakta hai jo bench ke apne exit code ko bekaar banate hain (failures 0 se exit, zero tests 0 se exit, bina summary ke crash).

Parser stdlib-only Python hai, noise ke counts print karta hai lekin kabhi `Message:` lines, tracebacks ki source lines ya locals nahi, aur documented provenance wale real captured output ke against tested hai.
`$module` aur `$test` shell tak pahunchne se pehle validate hote hain.
improvements: `--junit-xml-output` support jodo: check karo ki bench venv mein zaroori XML runner hai ya nahi aur text ki jagah XML parse karo.

Module 10 (`.claude/settings.json` ka owner) ko propose karo ki `permissions.allow` mein `Bash(cd /home/user/frappe-bench)` jode, taaki tester aur developer agents ke preloaded use ko prompt na chahiye.
Ek `--json` output mode jodo aur CI mein `structured_output` paane ke liye ise `claude -p --json-schema` ke saath use karo.

02-restrict-tools-and-hook.title: Reviewer ke tools restrict karo aur ek Claude Code hook ko uske liye scope karo
02-restrict-tools-and-hook.objective: Reviewer v1 par iterate karo: ek `tools` allowlist (koi Edit ya Write nahi), `permissionMode: dontAsk`, `maxTurns: 15`, verdict ke saath findings-table output, aur agent ke apne frontmatter mein ek `PreToolUse` Claude Code hook jodo jo sirf read-only git aur `bench --site test.localhost run-tests` allow kare, aur `bench console`, `execute` aur `migrate` block kare. Hook ko piped JSON se test karo, phir headless prove karo ki reviewer na bench console khol sakta hai na file edit kar sakta hai.
